headline: Alphabet-led tech rout and soft spending pull the 2-year down ~10bp; silver hits a 2026 low
summary: A record drop in Alphabet after weak AI-era sales sent the Nasdaq 100 down 1.4% and pushed money into Treasuries, so the 2-year fell about 10bp to near 4.60% and the 10-year about 8bp to 4.94% even though Q3 GDP beat at 3.4% and core PCE held at 3.1%. Crude gave back part of Wednesday's jump on US–Iran talk hopes, with WTI settling 0.8% lower at $102.00, while gold fell 1.1% to about $4,021 and silver 3.4% to a 2026 low near $52. The ECB held at 2.5% with a softer tone and Lagarde said she will leave on Feb 7, pulling the 2-year Schatz down about 6bp and keeping the OAT–Bund spread near 155bp.
drivers: AI jitters send money into bonds

Alphabet's record one-day fall on disappointing sales and heavy AI spending, plus 20%+ drops in ServiceNow and Fortinet, cut the Nasdaq 100 1.4%. Short Treasuries led the haven bid: the 2-year fell about 10bp to 4.60% and December hike odds slid to about 74% from 85%; Intel and Amazon after the bell extended the rally.

Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised against 3.1% expected and claims fell to 194,000, but September real spending and income missed and core PCE was in line at 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, with headline at 3.6% against 3.7% expected. Markets read it as no reason to add to December hike bets.
Iran: talks hopes against strike risk

Hopes for US–Iran peace talks pulled WTI and Brent down more than $2 intraday before reports of more attacks on Saudi energy sites and an IRGC claim that three tankers hit mines south of Hormuz trimmed the loss. WTI settled -0.8% at $102.00, Brent -0.4% at $114.88; a late WSJ report on Iran strike options lifted Brent after the settle.
A softer ECB hold and Lagarde's early exit

The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.5% unanimously after discussing a hike, stressing tighter financing conditions and no second-round effects; Lagarde will step down on Feb 7, 2027. The 2-year Schatz fell about 6bp to 3.05% and the 10-year Bund about 2.5bp to 3.36%, with the OAT–Bund spread near 155bp.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down 78¢ (-0.8%) at $102.00 after falling over $2 intraday; Brent -0.4% at $114.88.
oil.why: Crude gave back part of Wednesday's 3% jump as hopes for US–Iran peace talks took some fear out of the market, and both benchmarks were down more than $2 at the lows. The loss narrowed on reports of new attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and an IRGC claim that three tankers hit sea mines south of Hormuz. The Nasdaq rout weighed on risk appetite, but a late WSJ report that CENTCOM briefed Trump on Iran options lifted Brent after the settle.
oil.outlook: Range $97–106 with a firm bias into the Nov 3 midterms while strike talk persists. A US strike or confirmed Gulf supply loss would test $106 and the April high near $113; real talks with Tehran would let WTI slip toward $97.
oil.watch: Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and EIA data Nov 4.

gas.note: Nov RBOB rose 1.16¢ (+0.4%) to $3.1850 into Friday's expiry; Dec trades near $3.07. AAA pump average $4.22.
gas.why: The expiring November contract firmed slightly even as crude slipped, on expiry positioning before Friday and with Midwest stocks near record lows. The more active December contract traded about 1% lower near $3.07, reflecting last week's 3.9 million barrel gasoline build and weak late-season demand. Refiners are maximising diesel, whose margins are far richer, which keeps gasoline supply from tightening. AAA's national average fell another 2¢ to $4.22, down 5¢ in a week.
gas.outlook: Once December takes over, range $2.98–3.20. The crack is soft and demand seasonal, so gasoline should keep lagging crude; only a Gulf supply loss lifts it above $3.20, while another build would test $2.98.
gas.watch: Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, EIA stocks Nov 4 and Iran headlines.

gold.note: Spot fell about $47 (-1.1%) to near $4,021 after a $4,005 low; silver weakness and the dollar weighed overnight.
gold.why: Most of the drop came in Asian hours as the hawkish Fed hold and a firmer dollar hit bullion, and the strong 3.4% GDP print added pressure. Gold then failed to rally even as December hike odds fell from about 85% to 74% and the 2-year dropped about 10bp, a sign that funds are cutting length and selling gold to cover equity losses during the tech rout. The $4,000 level held by about $5.
gold.outlook: Range $3,950–4,100 with a soft bias while positioning clears. A daily close below $4,000 opens $3,940 near the year's low; a move back above $4,070 would show haven demand returning as yields fall.
gold.watch: Euro CPI Oct 30, the US midterms Nov 3, ISM Nov 2–4 and payrolls Nov 6.

silver.note: Spot fell about $1.82 (-3.4%) to near $52.15, its lowest futures close of 2026; gold/silver ratio up to 77.
silver.why: Silver fell almost three times as far as gold as rate-hike risk and the tech selloff hit its higher-beta, industrially exposed profile. It broke the $52.41 support in early New York trade, dropped to about $51.97 after the data and never recovered, while speculators keep cutting longs faster than in gold. It is now about 8.5% below its Oct 16 close and roughly 57% under January's record.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $50–55 range. A close below $51.40 points to $50; reclaiming $53.25 would signal the washout is over, most likely if yields keep falling and the ratio turns back from 77.
silver.watch: China PMIs Oct 31, US ISM manufacturing Nov 2 and payrolls Nov 6.

us2y.note: Down about 10bp to near 4.60%, its biggest fall in weeks, as December hike odds slid to about 74%.
us2y.why: The 2-year led the rally as the Alphabet-driven tech selloff sent money into short Treasuries and traders trimmed Fed hike bets. Data did not force the Fed's hand: core PCE matched forecasts at 3.1% and real spending and income missed, offsetting a 3.4% GDP beat. A dovish-leaning ECB hold added support, and weak Intel and Amazon results after the bell extended the move, with the yield near 4.57% in Asia.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.50–4.72%. December is still more likely than not, so a strong payrolls on Nov 6 would pull it back toward 4.70%; a deeper equity selloff or soft ISM could test 4.50%.
us2y.watch: ISM Nov 2, the midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us5y.note: Down roughly 7–8bp to the mid-4.7s, tracking the front end; near 4.70% in Asian trade.
us5y.why: The belly followed the 2-year lower as the tech rout and reduced Fed hike pricing outweighed strong growth data. A solid $44 billion 7-year auction, which stopped on the screws at 4.894% with 2.46 times cover and strong direct demand, showed investors are willing to buy intermediate duration near 5%. Lower oil and softer euro yields after the ECB helped.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.62–4.85%. It moves with December pricing: a weak equity tape and soft data favour 4.62%, a hot payrolls report or oil spike takes it back above 4.80%.
us5y.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us10y.note: Down about 8bp to near 4.94% from above 5%; slipped toward 4.90% in Asia as Nasdaq futures fell.
us10y.why: The 10-year dropped back below 5% as the Nasdaq 100's 1.4% slide on Alphabet's record fall and AI-spending worries revived the haven bid. Inflation data were in line, with core PCE at 3.1%, and spending missed, so the 3.4% GDP beat did not push yields up. Lower oil, a solid 7-year sale and falling European yields after the ECB added support; the curve steepened as the front end led.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.85–5.05%. Further tech losses or quiet midterms could test 4.85%; a heavier refunding on Nov 4 or a hot payrolls report would put 5.05% back in play.
us10y.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us30y.note: Down about 3–4bp to near 5.30%, lagging the front end as the curve steepened.
us30y.why: The long bond rallied least because the drivers of the day were Fed pricing and equity hedging, both of which favour shorter maturities. Term premium stays high on deficit worries, oil above $100 and inflation running at 3.6% headline, and investors are wary before next week's refunding. Microsoft's blowout $25 billion bond deal added to supply pressure on long duration.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.40%. Steepening is the path of least resistance; a larger coupon schedule on Nov 4 would push it toward 5.40%, while a risk-off break in stocks could pull it to 5.20%.
us30y.watch: The Nov 4 refunding, payrolls Nov 6 and the 30-year auction in mid-November.

de2y.note: Down about 5.6bp to near 3.05% after the ECB held at 2.5% with a softer tone.
de2y.why: The Schatz led the euro rally as the ECB held unanimously and Lagarde, while saying a hike was discussed, stressed relatively stable underlying inflation, no second-round effects and tighter financing conditions. Markets cut the odds of a December move, though some economists still expect one more hike to 2.75%. Lagarde's early exit on Feb 7 was seen as no change to the policy path.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.95–3.15%. The flash euro CPI on Oct 30, with September at 3.8%, is the next test: a hot print lifts it toward 3.15%, a soft one revives the 'done hiking' view and 2.95%.
de2y.watch: Euro CPI flash Oct 30, euro unemployment Nov 3 and ECB speakers.

de5y.note: Lower by about 4bp to near 3.13%, following the Schatz after the ECB.
de5y.why: The 5-year moved with the front end as investors trimmed ECB hike bets after a hold that Reuters described as less restrictive than September's meeting. Lagarde said euro-area 10-year yields are about 35bp higher than at the September projections, which does part of the tightening for the ECB. US Treasuries' rally later in the day added support.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.05–3.22%. Euro CPI and the US payrolls report set direction; a hot CPI would lift it toward 3.22%.
de5y.watch: Euro CPI Oct 30 and US payrolls Nov 6.

de10y.note: Down about 2.5bp to near 3.36%, with a 3.34% low after the ECB decision.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund fell in early trade with Treasuries after the Fed, then dipped to about 3.34% when the ECB held and avoided a strong hike signal. It lagged the 2-year as the curve steepened and some haven demand eased with the OAT spread stable. European stocks rallied on earnings, limiting the safe-haven bid.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.28–3.42%. A hot euro CPI or Brent above $120 would lift it toward 3.42%; a deeper US equity selloff or soft data would drag it to 3.28%.
de10y.watch: Euro CPI Oct 30, German retail sales and the US midterms Nov 3.

de30y.note: Little changed to slightly lower near 3.69%; the curve steepened as the front end rallied.
de30y.why: The long end lagged as the ECB's hold mostly repriced short rates, while long yields remain anchored by heavy euro-area supply, energy-driven inflation at 3.8% and global term-premium pressure from US Treasuries and gilts. UK gilts eased about 3–5bp after the budget, which limited spillover selling.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.78% with a steepening bias; a global long-end selloff around the US refunding is the main upside risk.
de30y.watch: The US refunding Nov 4, the BoE Nov 5 and German supply.

fr2y.note: Lower with Schatz after the ECB, near 3.6–3.65%; front-end OAT spread stable.
fr2y.why: French 2-year yields followed German ones lower as the ECB held at 2.5% and signalled caution, which reduced the risk of further hikes on top of the fiscal stress. Short OATs are less exposed to the budget fight than long ones, and Moody's hold last week still supports the front end.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.50–3.75%, led by ECB pricing; a failed budget vote would widen the spread more at long maturities than here.
fr2y.watch: French CPI and Q3 GDP flash Oct 30 and the budget vote around Nov 3.

fr5y.note: Lower by a few bp after the ECB, tracking Bunds; spread to Germany broadly unchanged.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT moved with the core curve as the ECB's softer hold pushed short and medium yields down. It did not outperform because the spread is still driven by politics: parliament has yet to pass the 2027 budget, and the market is weighing Lagarde's early exit, which lets Macron influence her successor before the 2027 election.
fr5y.outlook: Bias for a stable spread to Bunds in a 5–10bp band unless the budget vote fails; outright direction follows euro CPI and the ECB.
fr5y.watch: French CPI Oct 30, the budget vote around Nov 3 and the Nov 19 medium-term OAT auction.

fr10y.note: Near 4.90%, a low of 4.83% after the ECB; spread to Bunds about 155bp, versus a 177bp peak on Oct 22.
fr10y.why: The 10-year OAT outperformed in the morning and briefly fell about 10bp after the ECB, as Lagarde avoided a hike that strategists said would have added to OAT stress. Part of the gain faded into the close as investors weighed her early exit, linked by many to France's 2027 election, and Lagarde's stance that France must fix its own fiscal problem rather than rely on the ECB.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 145–165bp, centred near 155bp. A failed budget vote or political crisis would push it back toward 170bp; budget progress could narrow it toward 145bp.
fr10y.watch: French GDP and CPI Oct 30, budget vote around Nov 3, Nov 5 OAT auction and S&P's Nov 27 review.

fr30y.note: Near 5.4%, little changed; the long-end spread to Germany stays wide near 170–180bp.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT lagged the rally because the long end carries the most fiscal risk premium, and the ECB said nothing that would support it. With debt near 118% of GDP, a divided parliament still working on the 2027 budget and a national strike planned for Nov 5, investors keep demanding extra yield at long maturities.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.30–5.55% with an upside bias into the budget vote and the Nov 5 long-term OAT auction; a smooth vote would ease it toward 5.30%.
fr30y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, the Nov 5 auction and strike, and S&P Nov 27.

watch: Next: euro and French CPI, French GDP, the BoJ, and Nov RBOB and Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ Nov 1, the US midterms and French budget vote Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding, the BoE and OAT auction Nov 5, and payrolls Nov 6.
sources: Dow Jones via MarketScreener (ECB, euro bonds)
